must_find.item: Women survived at a much higher rate than men (about 74% against 19%).
must_find.quote: Women survived at 74.2% (233 of 314) compared with 18.9% for men (109 of 577).
must_find.reason: States the female and male survival rates with the correct direction and numbers.

must_find.item: Survival falls with passenger class, highest in first class and lowest in third.
must_find.reason: Survival falls with class from first to third, with the rates given.

must_find.item: Passengers who survived had paid higher fares on average.
must_find.quote: Fare: survivors have mean £48.40 and median 26.0. Non-survivors have mean 22.12 and median 10.5.
must_find.reason: Survivors paid higher fares on average, and the report says so with numbers.

must_find.item: Passengers without a recorded cabin survived less often than those with one.
must_find.quote: survival is 30.0% when Cabin is missing versus 66.7% when present (p = 6.7e-21)
must_find.reason: Missing cabin is linked to lower survival, with the numbers given.

must_find.item: Passengers with a missing Age survived less often than those with a recorded Age.
must_find.quote: survival is 29.4% when Age is missing versus 40.6% when present (p = 0.008)
must_find.reason: Missing Age is linked to lower survival, with the numbers given.

must_find.item: A predictive model is compared with the majority-class baseline (about 62% accuracy) and beats it.
must_find.quote: Logistic regression reaches 77.6% test accuracy and ROC AUC 0.841, against 61.4% for a majority-class baseline.
must_find.reason: The model is compared with the majority-class baseline of about 61% and beats it.

must_find.item: Model results include precision, recall or F1, not only accuracy.
must_find.reason: The results table includes precision, recall and F1 as well as accuracy.

must_not_claim.quote: Of the passengers, 549 (61.6%) did not survive and 342 (38.4%) did.
must_not_claim.reason: The report says most passengers did not survive, which contradicts the claim.

must_not_claim.item: Men survived at a higher rate than women.
must_not_claim.quote: Women survived at 74.2% (233 of 314) compared with 18.9% for men (109 of 577).
must_not_claim.reason: The report shows women surviving more than men, the opposite of the claim.

must_not_claim.item: Third-class passengers survived at a higher rate than first-class passengers.
must_not_claim.reason: The report says third class had lower survival than first class, the opposite of the claim.

must_not_claim.item: Age is the strongest predictor of survival.
must_not_claim.quote: Age is borderline and not significant after family-level correction (Holm p = 0.082).
must_not_claim.reason: The report says Sex is the dominant predictor and treats Age as borderline and not significant.

caveats.quote: Cabin is missing for 77.1% of passengers and Age for 19.9%.
caveats.reason: The report flags missing cabin as a data quality limitation and says it was not used in any model.
